_readme: THE strobe registry. Every strobe name a task spec may reference is declared here,
and the compiler resolves names to numbers against this file and nothing else.
APPEND-ONLY IS A HARD RULE, NOT A CONVENTION. Downstream analysis depends on codes
and their ordering, and historical comparability is a hard requirement. A code is
never repurposed, never renumbered, never deleted. Adding one means: pick the next
free number from `free_ranges`, give it a `rationale`, and bump nothing -- adding a
code does not bump `vocab_version`, because additions cannot break an existing spec.
`vocab_version` bumps only if this file's SHAPE changes.
SOURCE OF TRUTH. Codes with origin 'firmware' mirror BehaviorBox.h:97-129 and their
numbers are fixed by ~4 years of recorded sessions. Codes with origin 'taskgraph'
are new in this project. Once the generator in Phase 1 exists, this file emits the
firmware header, the compiler's table, and a task.json-shaped strobes{} map, which
retires the three-way hand-mirroring described in PHASE0_PLAN.md section 1.3.
DECLARED MEANS EMITTABLE. Ephymeris docs/tasks.md:207-213 records a real bug where
GRGL_Sim declared 23 of 31 codes and emitted codes it had not declared; nothing
errored and each layer degraded silently. The inverse is equally a bug: do not add
a code here on a hunch that something might want it one day.
The rule used to read DECLARED MEANS EMITTED, and named the shipped specs as the
witnesses. Nothing ships as a spec now, and the port-slot codes below are emitted
by a construction the compiler supports rather than by a file in this repository:
the moment an operator wires a third response port, slot 3's six codes are what
that port reports with. That is a different thing from speculation, and the test
is whether a code has a mechanism that produces it, not whether a file already
does. WATCHDOG_FAULT has carried `emitted_by: []` under exactly this reasoning
since Phase 1 -- the runtime produces it, no graph does.
PORT SLOTS. `port_slots` below maps a response port's slot number to the six
codes it reports with. Slots 1 and 2 are the historical _L and _R families, so
the recorded archive decodes unchanged; 3-7 are new. A response channel declares
its slot in channels.v1.json, which is what lets the compiler stop knowing about
left and right. Seven is not a preference: TG_MAX_WATCH is 8 and one watchable
channel is the engagement port.
_code_max_why: emitStrobe formats "%03d\t%lu" (BehaviorBox.h:275-281) and the host's IN_SESSION
parser is ^\d{1,3}\t\d+$ -- so a 4-digit code is unparseable on the host and
silently dropped. 999 is a wire-format limit, not a preference.
Five codes already exceed 255 (256, 257, 258, 357, 369), so the compiled state
table stores strobes as uint16. See docs/decisions.md D5.
_free_ranges_why: Gaps in the firmware numbering. Non-contiguous and non-patterned, which is why the compiler must look codes up rather than compute them. NOTE the 107-220 gap is split around 110-113: those are retired, not free -- see `retired` below.

START_SESSION.rationale: Anchors every timestamp in the run. Emitted by the sketch loop, not by a trial node.

LIGHTS_ON.emitted_on: entry to the engagement window (trial cue on)
LIGHTS_ON.rationale: The trial-available edge. Paired with nothing; its partner LIGHTS_OFF is not.

LAZY_RAT.rationale: Abstention. No stimulus was presented, so the trial carries no evidence about discrimination and is scored invalid. See BehaviorBox.h:1158-1159.

ODOR_POKE.rationale: Separates an incidental beam-break from a committed initiation. NOTE: does NOT clear the abstention escalator -- BehaviorBox.h:1171-1174 closed that loophole deliberately.

ODOR_UNPOKE_EARLY.rationale: A commitment or sampling hold released early. Emitted from two distinct firmware sites (BehaviorBox.h:1181 pre-odor, :1197 sampling) with the same code, so the two are indistinguishable downstream. See open question in docs/spikes/avr-ram.md.

ODOR_UNPOKE.emitted_on: entry to the response window, after a complete sample
ODOR_UNPOKE.rationale: Withdrawal from the odor port is the sampling/response boundary. The pair order is INVERTED relative to the three abort paths (BehaviorBox.h:1210 then :1213) -- this is why paired strobes are modelled as ordered nodes rather than as a set. See docs/decisions.md D2.

LIGHTS_OFF.emitted_on: entry to a zero-duration node that clears the trial light
LIGHTS_OFF.rationale: Always co-emitted with a behavioural code, never alone, and its ORDER relative to that partner varies by path. Modelled as its own zero-duration node so the order is authored rather than implicit.

INVALID_TRIAL.rationale: The counter does not advance and the same trial binding is re-presented, so an unsampled trial never enters the record as a choice. Emitted by the sketch loop today, not by runTrial().

END_CORRECT_ITI.rationale: Scores correct, advances the counter, clears penalty escalation. Kept distinct from END_INCORRECT_ITI so reinforcement rate and timeout cost are separable.

END_INCORRECT_ITI.rationale: Reached by THREE distinct outcomes -- wrong port, omission, and response-hold failure (BehaviorBox.h:1225) -- so outcome class is NOT recoverable from this code alone. It is recoverable from the preceding strobe, which is exactly why the invariant matters.

END_SESSION.rationale: The clean-stop sentinel. Ephymeris keys its only hardcoded strobe string off this (sessions/runner.py:36).

ODOR_OFF.emitted_on: entry to the sampling-release WAIT_EXIT, and to an inter-stimulus gap
ODOR_OFF.rationale: Odor cleared and vacuum reopened. Reused for the inter-stimulus gap in chained-sampling tasks: the emitter-off event is the same physical event.

WATER_POKE_L.emitted_on: entry to the response branch node, left channel
WATER_POKE_L.rationale: Emitted BEFORE correctness is known (BehaviorBox.h:1082 vs :1093). This is why the response branch is its own zero-duration node with the guard on its edges. See docs/decisions.md D3. Doubles as the false-alarm code on go/no-go.

WATER_POKE_R.emitted_on: entry to the response branch node, right channel

WATER_UNPOKE_EARLY_L.emitted_on: entry to the response-hold-failure penalty, left
WATER_UNPOKE_EARLY_L.rationale: The correct port was reached but released before the hold completed -- a consummatory failure, not a wrong choice. Scored separately so it never contaminates the discrimination measure.

WATER_UNPOKE_EARLY_R.emitted_on: entry to the response-hold-failure penalty, right

FLUID_L.emitted_on: entry to the left reward PULSE
FLUID_L.rationale: Emitted before the solenoid opens (BehaviorBox.h:1047). Pulse width is the delivered volume.

FLUID_R.emitted_on: entry to the right reward PULSE

WATER_UNPOKE_L.emitted_on: entry to the ITI delay, after leaving the left well
WATER_UNPOKE_L.rationale: The only place the firmware observes the end of a consummatory bout, which makes it the anchor for consumption-duration measures. Not emitted on a wrong-well answer -- BehaviorBox.h:1108-1113 returns immediately without awaiting withdrawal.

WATER_UNPOKE_R.emitted_on: entry to the ITI delay, after leaving the right well

WATER_POKE_NONE.emitted_on: entry to the correct terminal path on a withhold trial
WATER_POKE_NONE.rationale: Correct withholding. Already fully implemented in firmware (BehaviorBox.h:1115-1133) although no shipped sketch instantiates isGo=false today, so go/no-go reuses an existing code rather than needing a new one.

WATER_POKE_ERROR_L.emitted_on: entry to the wrong-port penalty, left
WATER_POKE_ERROR_L.rationale: A genuine discrimination error: sampling completed and a choice was expressed, so it advances the session rather than repeating.

WATER_POKE_ERROR_R.emitted_on: entry to the wrong-port penalty, right

STOP_FLUID_G_R.emitted_on: entry to the right consumption WAIT_EXIT
STOP_FLUID_G_R.rationale: Emitted after the solenoid closes (BehaviorBox.h:1051). Modelling it as the entry strobe of the consumption state colocates the actuator close with its strobe -- semantically tidier than the current bracketing, and free.

STOP_FLUID_G_L.emitted_on: entry to the left consumption WAIT_EXIT

ODOR_1_ON.emitted_on: entry to a sampling HOLD bound to odor line 1
ODOR_1_ON.rationale: Stimulus identity. This is the one state whose entry code identifies WHAT was presented, which is why it is a per-trial @binding rather than a fixed field.

ODOR_2_ON.emitted_on: entry to a sampling HOLD bound to odor line 2

ODOR_3_ON.emitted_on: entry to a sampling HOLD bound to odor line 3

ODOR_4_ON.emitted_on: entry to a sampling HOLD bound to odor line 4

ODOR_5_ON.emitted_on: entry to a sampling HOLD bound to odor line 5

ODOR_6_ON.emitted_on: entry to a sampling HOLD bound to odor line 6

RETENTION_ON.emitted_on: entry to the unfilled retention delay
RETENTION_ON.rationale: NEW. The working-memory load in delayed match-to-sample and sequence designs. No firmware code exists because no shipped task has a retention delay. Numbered 260 -- immediately after the last firmware code in the 24x block -- so the new taskgraph codes read as a contiguous group.

INTERSTIM_GAP_ON.emitted_on: entry to the gap between chained stimuli
INTERSTIM_GAP_ON.rationale: NEW. Distinguishes the inter-stimulus gap from the post-sampling ODOR_OFF: both clear the emitter, but only one is followed by another stimulus. Without a distinct code, a 2-stage trial and a 1-stage trial are ambiguous in the stream.

RESP_OMIT.rationale: NEW. Firmware used to emit NOTHING when the response window expired, so an omission was only inferable from the absence of a poke before END_INCORRECT_ITI. Firmware now emits it (docs/firmware-changes.md #2), and so does the model. The as-built fixture tests/fixtures/grgl_2odor_asbuilt.yaml still reproduces the silence, because that is what the recorded corpus was produced by. See docs/decisions.md D4.

WATCHDOG_FAULT.emitted_on: a state exceeding its maximum dwell; the session then ends
WATCHDOG_FAULT.rationale: NEW. Emitted by the SESSION LAYER, not by a node -- like START_SESSION and INVALID_TRIAL, and for the same reason: it reports something about the run rather than about a state entry, so routing it through tgEnterNode() would break the one-state-one-strobe invariant that makes every other timestamp a state-entry time. `emitted_by` is empty because no spec's graph produces it; the runtime does, and only when something has gone wrong. Its absence from a session is the normal case and is the evidence that no state overran.

WATER_POKE_P3.emitted_on: entry to the response branch node, port 3

Unemitted on a rig with fewer than 3 response ports, which is the normal case -- see this file's _readme on DECLARED MEANS EMITTABLE. _why: Slot -> the six codes a response port on that slot reports with.
Slots 1 and 2 point at the historical _L and _R names, so a recorded session
decodes exactly as it always did and the archive is untouched. Everything
above them is uniform. A response channel names its slot in channels.v1.json.
This table is why nothing in the compiler derives a code from a channel called
'left_well'. It used to: paradigms.py carried _SIDE = {left_well: _L, ...} and
operations.ts carried a matching sideSuffix(), so a box whose wells were named
anything else silently got no per-port codes at all.

_readme: Codes that were emitted by firmware this repository no longer contains, and
which MUST NOT be reused. Append-only means a code is never repurposed, and
that applies just as much to a code whose emitter is gone: 24,600 recorded
events carry these, and reissuing one would silently merge two unrelated
event types in any analysis that spans the boundary.
They are not in `codes` because nothing emits them, and the linter requires
every declared code to be emitted. They are not in `free_ranges` because they
are not free. This section is the third state.
The replay validator recognises them by name so a legacy session reports
'retired code' rather than 'unknown code' -- a distinction that matters,
because one is explained and the other is a question.

DUMMY_SOLENOID_CLICK_1.rationale: Dummy solenoid click. Emitted between a terminal and the next LIGHTS_ON to mask the audible cue of the real odor valve, so a subject could not use valve noise to predict the trial.
